title: India AI Governance Guidelines
summary: MeitY released the India AI Governance Guidelines under the IndiaAI Mission on 5 November 2025, building on a draft report on AI governance guidelines development put out for comment in January 2025. The guidelines set out seven principles ('sutras'), recommendations across six pillars, and a short-, medium- and long-term action plan. They conclude that a separate AI law is not needed for now and rely on existing laws, sector regulators and voluntary measures. They recommend an inter-ministerial AI Governance Group, a Technology and Policy Expert Committee, a role for the AI Safety Institute, a national AI incident database, and IT Act amendments on liability and safe harbour.
key_obligations: Start with voluntary commitments, with binding mandates possibly later
Report AI incidents to a national database (recommended)
Use techno-legal tools such as watermarking and content authentication
Graded liability proportionate to each actor's role and risk

sources.title: MeitY unveils India AI Governance Guidelines under IndiaAI Mission
